newsitem.title: USA: Bridgestone unit to build $400 million U.S. plant.
newsitem.headline: Bridgestone unit to build $400 million U.S. plant.

text.p: Japan's Bridgestone Corp. said Monday that its Bridgestone/Firestone unit plans to build a $400 million passenger and light truck tire manufacturing plant in the United States.

The location of the new plant has not yet been determined, but Bridgestone/Firestone said in a statement that it has narrowed its choice to several sites in different states and will make a decision shortly.
The company said that no additional sites will be considered at this time and no further comment concerning site selection will be made until the ultimate site is determined.

"Bridgestone/Firestone has enjoyed four straight years of improved market share and sales, and we are determined to build on this momentum," said Bridgestone/Firestone Chief Executive Officer Masatoshi Ono.

"We need this new plant to satisfy the strong demand for our products," he said. "Also, we want to reduce our imports from Japan. The majority of tires that we sell in America are made here now, but we want to increase our domestic production even more."

Last December, Bridgestone/Firestone said that it will spend $430 million in 1997-98 at existing plants in the United States and Canada to expand annual production of passenger and light truck tires by 4.7 million units.
Construction will begin immediately after the site is selected, and production is slated to begin in the spring of 1999, it said.

The plant is expected to reach production of 25,000 radial passenger and light truck tires per day in the year 2000, employing 300 to 400 people when production begins, with employment reaching 800 people in the year 2000, the company said.
